children: Iondrive
has entered Oklahoma’s formal incentive qualification process for its first commercial rare earth recycling module after the state accepted its Quality Jobs application.
The proposed operation could qualify for approximately US$5.2 million in state and local benefits within a broader incentive framework potentially exceeding US$15m across three modules.
The move advances an opportunity first identified by the Oklahoma Department of Commerce in June, when the state provided preliminary estimates and a letter of support.
While the application has been received and date-stamped, no incentive has been approved and any eventual benefits will depend on eligibility and operating performance.
Established State Procedures
Completion of Iondrive’s US entity registrations allowed its Quality Jobs application to be accepted for processing, fixing the relevant application date and beginning established state procedures.
The next stages involve an eligibility determination and negotiation of an applicable incentive agreement rather than the automatic release of funding.
Quality Jobs payroll rebates form part of the proposed support alongside eligible state and local tax incentives and workforce training assistance.
These measures are intended to reduce the effective cost of establishing and operating the facility but are performance-based rather than upfront construction cash.
Access will depend on the operation meeting employment, investment and other applicable program requirements, with similar arrangements potentially available for later modules.
Parallel Additional Funding
Iondrive is separately seeking support through Oklahoma’s Governor’s Quick Action Closing Fund, a discretionary initiative outside the estimated three-module incentive package.

It is also exploring federal, state, and Tribal Nation assistance that could provide cash grants, site and infrastructure support, or other eligible project funding, each of which requires separate assessment and approval..

The company is also pursuing a targeted US$18m senior debt facility under the US Department of Agriculture Business & Industry Guaranteed Loan Program, potentially guaranteeing up to 80% of qualifying lender exposure.
“Our job is to get the first module into commercial operation and build a business that can expand from there,” chief executive officer Dr Grant Caffery said.
Ongoing Commercial Preparations
Alongside funding discussions, the company is advancing module engineering, establishment of its US operating business, and engagement with prospective feedstock suppliers and product customers.

The initial facility would use its IONSolv metal extraction platform, based on deep eutectic solvent chemistry, which Iondrive is developing for selective recovery of critical minerals from multiple feedstocks.
Iondrive intends to complete the remaining Quality Jobs steps while progressing the discretionary funding applications, lender discussions and engineering work.
No grant or guarantee has yet been awarded, and the first commercial module still requires engineering, permitting, financing, and a final investment decision by the board.

title: Iondrive Enters Oklahoma Incentive Process for First Recycling Module
